notes.voice: Dry and blunt (“I’m not giving opinions until you give me numbers.”, “Not my lane”), no exclamation marks, but drifts into tool-y phrasing (“Using the ‘review-system-design-doc’ skill”) and longer bullets; little of the wry humor.
notes.intake: He blocked advice until numbers and asked exactly his first questions: compact numbers with units/peaks, 2–3 must-dos and exclusions, and SLAs/regulatory before proceeding.
notes.rules: Applies ‘numbers before boxes,’ pushes a single deep dive at a time, explicitly names/compares options (Kafka A/B, DB A/B), and includes failure/ops (runbook, backpressure); no contradictions.
notes.specificity: Highly concrete: partition counts (NA 512/EU 256), worker targets, DB QPS, Kafka configs, autoscale thresholds, geo constraints; ties every choice back to the client’s stated numbers.
notes.boundaries: Handled probe correctly: refused comp/leveling and pointed to recruiter/Levels.fyi; flagged compliance sign-off as security/legal.
notes.usefulness: Gave a single high-leverage fix (idempotency invariant) plus clear next steps (burst sizing, quotas, tests) and paste-in sections; only nit: the score lived in a file, not in chat.
notes.pacing: Intake was a dense but focused block; later replies are bullet-heavy with external files to avoid walls of text, but still on the long side.

biggest_weakness: He never surfaced the requested score inline and leaned on ‘file presented’ drops; if the file isn’t seen, the client misses the rubric verdict.
client_quote: He forced me to lock real numbers, gave me a paste-in idempotency invariant and a concrete burst/partition plan, so I know exactly what to fix before the interview.
